claims.text: A short anneal near 600 °C will induce nanoscale BCC precipitates in a predominantly B2 AlCoFeNi-based alloy.
A short anneal near 600 °C may induce D03-like precipitates in a predominantly B2 AlCoFeNi-based alloy.
The anneal-induced precipitates and their interfaces will increase magnetic domain-wall pinning.
Increased domain-wall pinning will increase the field required to move domain walls and thereby raise coercivity.
The annealed alloy will have a coercive field 2–3 times that of the matched as-prepared or solution-treated baseline.
The initial as-cast or solution-treated AlCoFeNi-based alloy has a predominantly B2 matrix.
The intervention is annealing at approximately 600 °C for 1–2 hours under inert gas or vacuum.
The baseline is predominantly single-phase B2.
The baseline has minimal domain-wall pinning centers.
Lower annealing temperatures can cause AlCoFeNi to decompose into ordered B2 and disordered BCC phases.
The length scale of B2/BCC decomposition depends on alloy composition and annealing temperature.
The optimal annealing time and temperature may vary with slight compositional changes and processing route.
The coercivity enhancement should be most pronounced in alloys that form stable nanoscale precipitates during moderate-temperature annealing.
If nanoscale precipitates do not form, the coercivity enhancement may be reduced or absent.
Matched baseline and annealed samples will be compared by room-temperature hysteresis measurements and electron microscopy.
The hypothesis is considered falsified if coercivity after annealing does not exceed 1.5 times baseline or if no nanoscale precipitates are detected.

contradictions.description: The prediction requires a 2–3× coercivity increase, but the falsification rule only rejects increases of 1.5× or less. Results between 1.5× and 2× would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
